output.summary: KEP-5501 proposes that the kube-scheduler update a Pod's status conditions with the rejection message when a PreEnqueue plugin rejects it, using the new reason NotReadyForScheduling, via a delayed asynchronous API call behind the SchedulerPreEnqueuePodStatus feature gate. The KEP is in implementable status at stage beta.
output.rationale:
Pods rejected at PreEnqueue stay in a generic Pending state with no status feedback, which makes debugging hard, especially for transparent plugins like DRA. The design reuses framework.Status messages and applies a 5-second delayed dispatch with message de-duplication to limit API server load. It depends on SchedulerAsyncAPICalls so status patches do not block the scheduling loop.</rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">null

alternatives.option: Actively clearing the message when the rejecting plugin no longer rejects the Pod
alternatives.why_not: The readme's alternatives discussion notes it could cause confusion if the condition appears and disappears while the Pod remains Pending for another reason, and it adds API calls.

alternatives.option: Reporting via the existing Unschedulable condition or a new condition, with the CA processing such Pods
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers concluded PreEnqueue rejections relate to the Pod itself, not nodes, so Unschedulable would make the Cluster Autoscaler process pods it cannot fix; a new reason NotReadyForScheduling was chosen instead.

alternatives.option: Plugin opt-out from reporting (nil reasons) or per-plugin delay passed via PreEnqueueResult
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers (sanposhiho) argued opting out would hide why pods are stuck, and the author moved to an implicit, framework-level delay with no opt-out.

alternatives.option: Keep SchedulingGated status solely via kube-apiserver
alternatives.why_not: Kept as a unified-message approach, so the scheduler skips redundant patches; moving it fully to kube-scheduler was left as an investigation because it would need a distinct reason and could add API calls.

evidence.quote: If the delay period expires, the scheduler will asynchronously patch the Pod's status with the last-captured rejection message, using the new reason `NotReadyForScheduling`.
The enablement of this feature will be dependent on the `SchedulerAsyncAPICalls` feature gate being enabled, as the asynchronous patching mechanism is critical to protect scheduler throughput.
I think just the approach with delays ("Implicit + Delayed (No opt-out)") might be the best and simple solution.
I think I was wrong with the CA use case and the PreEnqueue rejection shouldn't be processed by the CA
If we are unable to re-enable async API calls in v1.35, the reflect PreEnqueue feature will remain disabled by default (in alpha or beta).
